skill.name: doc-coauthoring
skill.description: Guides users through a structured workflow for drafting, refining, and reader-testing documentation with AI assistance.
skill.summary: Coauthor structured documentation through context gathering, section drafting, iterative edits, and reader testing.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Long documents often lose context, structure, and reader focus during drafting. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through context gathering, section refinement, and reader testing.
actual_capabilities: Guides context gathering with audience, impact, template, and constraint questions.
Turns user notes into section-by-section document structures with placeholders.
Brainstorms candidate points for each section before drafting.
Refines sections through targeted replacement edits instead of full rewrites.
Tests documents with a fresh model or manual Claude.ai review prompts.
Checks drafts for flow, redundancy, contradictions, and unclear assumptions.
limitations: It does not verify factual accuracy, links, or technical claims by itself.
Connector use depends on available integrations and user permission.
Manual reader testing is required when sub-agents are unavailable.
The workflow can be slower than freeform drafting for short notes.

use_cases.title: Draft Technical Specs
use_cases.description: Build a clear technical spec from rough architecture notes, constraints, and stakeholder concerns.

use_cases.title: Shape Decision Docs
use_cases.description: Turn scattered tradeoffs into a structured decision document that explains the recommendation and alternatives.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reader Testing
use_cases.description: Test whether a draft answers realistic reader questions before sharing it with a wider audience.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me coauthor a document. Ask me for the document type, audience, desired impact, format, and key constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Raw Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after sharing notes or meeting context.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have shared raw context for this document. Identify what is clear, what is missing, and the first sections we should draft.

prompt_templates.title: Refine One Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a single section through focused iteration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Work on the next section only. Ask clarifying questions, brainstorm possible points, then draft a concise version for review.

prompt_templates.title: Run Reader Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before publishing the document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as a fresh reader with no prior context. Generate realistic questions, check whether the document answers them, and list gaps to fix.

output_examples.input: I need a decision doc for a new billing migration.
output: The assistant asks about audience, desired decision, alternatives, migration risks, and required format.
It proposes sections for context, goals, options, recommendation, rollout, and risks.

output_examples.input: Here are rough notes for the technical approach section.
output: The assistant asks targeted questions about dependencies, edge cases, rollout order, and failure modes.
It drafts the section and asks for specific edits before moving forward.

output_examples.input: Test whether this proposal is ready for executives.
output: The assistant predicts reader questions about business impact, risk, cost, ownership, and timing.
It reports unclear assumptions and recommends focused fixes.

best_practices: Share audience, purpose, constraints, and known tradeoffs before drafting begins.
Review each section after targeted edits so the assistant learns your style.
Run reader testing before sharing important documents with stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Skipping context gathering and asking for a final document immediately.
Using the full workflow for a short note that only needs light editing.
Letting the assistant invent missing facts instead of marking gaps.

faq.question: What types of documents does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports technical specs, decision docs, proposals, RFCs, PRDs, and similar structured documents.

faq.question: Does it write the whole document at once?
faq.answer: No. It builds the document section by section so each part can be reviewed and improved.

faq.question: Can it use shared documents or team channels?
faq.answer: Yes, when the host tool has the right integrations and the user approves access.

faq.question: What is reader testing?
faq.answer: Reader testing checks whether a fresh model can understand the document without the author context.

faq.question: Is this useful in Codex or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide file-based drafting, targeted edits, and sub-agent review when those tools are available.

faq.question: Does it guarantee factual accuracy?
faq.answer: No. Users still need to verify facts, links, technical details, and final document quality.
